gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's SOLIX F3800 Plus shuts off its 240 V output while it charges from 120 V AC, so recharging it from a wall outlet or a 120 V-only generator stops a 240 V well pump. To keep the pump running while a gas generator refills the battery, the generator must be 240 V and connected through Anker's 240V Bypass Charging Cable (Generator Input Adapter) at the F3800 Plus's Home Power Panel port.
standout_why: Compared against offgridbenchmark.com/learn/generator-for-well-pump (2026-11-02), holdbackup.com/guides/portable-generator-for-well-pump and thewell.guide/guides/generator-for-well-pump. Offgridbenchmark names the F3800 Plus but only marks it '240 V yes' and says it 'cannot say' whether it starts any motor; it does not mention L14-30, 14-50 or any transfer-switch pairing. HoldBackup and The Well Guide cover 240 V outlets, L14-30 inlets and transfer switches only for gas generators, and neither names a power station. None says a battery's 240 V output can switch off depending on how it is being charged, or which generator voltage and adapter keep the pump running during a long outage. That decides which charging part goes in the set.
kit_items: Battery power station: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus. It has a 120/240 V L14-30R outlet rated 25 A / 6,000 W, which can feed a 240 V well-pump circuit through a transfer switch.

Transfer switch: Anker's 10-Circuit Manual Transfer Switch (Reliance Pro/Tran 2, 50 A, 120/240 V). Anker lists it for the F3800 and F3800 Plus, and it has a 20 A 2-pole and a 30 A 2-pole circuit, so it can carry a 240 V pump. Anker's 6-circuit switch is excluded: Anker lists it as 120 V with an L5-30 inlet and 15 A single-pole circuits only, for the F3000/F2600/F2000.

Generator charging link: Anker SOLIX 240V Bypass Charging Cable (Generator Input Adapter). It takes a 240 V generator's L14-30 output into the F3800 Plus's Home Power Panel port, which allows charging and 240 V output at the same time. With a 120 V generator (through a TT-30 adapter) or the 120 V wall charger, the 240 V output, and so the pump, is unavailable while charging.
Optional extra battery: Anker SOLIX BP3800 (3,840 Wh). Anker's adapter FAQ says it raises charging from a 240 V generator from 3,300 W to 6,000 W.

findings.label: L14-30R output rating
findings.value: 120/240 V, 25 A, 6,000 W max (total AC output 6,000 W)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page (tech specs)
findings.note: The NEMA 5-20R outlets are 120 V, 20 A, 2,400 W max. The TT-30R is 120 V, 3,000 W. Anker lists no surge or peak watts.

findings.label: 120 V generator connection
findings.value: TT-30R only, up to 3,000 W; generator must be pure sine wave with THD under 5%
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus product page (FAQ)
findings.note: A 240 V generator connects through the Home Power Panel/Generator Adapter port. Anker says the Generator Adapter 'only support[s] single F3800 Plus unit'.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX 240V Bypass Charging Cable / Generator Input Adapter
findings.label: Generator connection and simultaneous output
findings.value: L14-30P to the generator, into the F3800 Plus's Home Power Panel port. Charging and powering loads at the same time is supported. Max input is 3,000 W at 120 V or 6,000 W at 240 V. Recharging from a 240 V generator is 3,300 W max, or 6,000 W with expansion batteries.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX 240V Bypass Charging Cable for F3800 Plus
findings.note: The page title says 'Bypass Charging Cable' but its FAQ calls the product the 'Generator Input Adapter'. Per the FAQ, a 120 V generator needs a TT-30 to L14-30R adapter, and the Home Power Panel needs a 240 V generator. A 14-50 generator needs an L14-30R to 14-50P adapter. The NEMA 5-20R outlets are disabled while it is connected. It must not be connected to the grid. It requires an L1+L2+N+PE system at 60 Hz.
